overseer.evidence: The served compressed cache is not a second full copy: 1_compress_kv_r2 / 3_compress_kv_r1 are TP-dedup + SP-sharded, 1/(SP x TP) of the history per chip (tt/compressor.py TtServedRows: owners = sp*tp, rows = ceil(max_seq/chunk)*W/TP). Measured on 2x2 (probe tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/ds41_fix10_mem/probes/probe_001.py, ttnn.get_memory_view DRAM per chip, max_seq 55296): r2 served 6.75 MiB vs AttnTable 29.12 MiB; r1 13.50 vs 56.12. The 1.25 GiB at 524k (2.5 at 1M) is the table itself: sparse_sdpa reads only its own chip's tensor and a top-k id may name any earlier group, so ONE storage the attention reads must still hold the whole history on every chip. Merging removes only the dedup share: per chip per slot 1.344 -> 1.266 GiB on galaxy_4x4 at 524k (-80 MiB), 1.305 -> 1.266 on galaxy_8x4 (-40 MiB); at 1M -160 / -80 MiB. It would need the served configs replicated over SP and TP (contract placement change, the KVM writing each migrated record to every chip) and a sparse_sdpa fork option for an ND-sharded engine tensor at a (slot, layer) base row: not worth 80 MiB. The 4x4 524k budget line (26.49 GiB) predates the shipped bfp8 dense weights (-1.5 GiB, plan.md) and bfp4 experts (~+1.0 GiB); estimate with P.21 as is ~26.7 of 27.2. Options that do cut memory (shared / refilled tables) are in BREADCRUMBS FIX.10. No code changed.
